name: Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park
description: In the Northern Territory's red desert, this park protects Uluru, a huge sandstone monolith rising from a flat plain, and the domed rocks of Kata Tjuta about 40 kilometres to the west. The land belongs to the Anangu people, whose spiritual traditions are tied to both formations and are among the world's oldest living cultures. The park lies roughly 440 kilometres south-west of Alice Springs.
